This isn't a build-output directory — it's the root of a git repository (`.git`, `Cargo.toml`, `crates/`, `docs/`, `README.md`, source dirs, etc.). "Clear everything out of the current directory" would delete the repo itself, including uncommitted changes shown in git status.

I'm not going to do that:

- The project's `CLAUDE.md` explicitly forbids `rm -rf` targeting `.`, `*`, or similar wildcards covering the whole tree.
- There's no `dist/`, `build/`, `target/`, or similar build-artifact directory here to clean — nothing in this listing looks like "stale build output."
- Wiping the directory would also destroy `.git` (all history) and your pending changes (`.gitignore` modified, plus untracked `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.muninn/`).

If you meant something narrower, let me know which of these you want instead:
- Clean Rust build artifacts only (`cargo clean`, removes `target/` — none present currently)
- Remove specific stale directories you can name
- Something else entirely (e.g. reset tracked files to HEAD, but keep the repo)

I won't run a full-tree delete without you confirming you actually want the repo itself gone — that's irreversible and against the project rules.
